To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Yard-Sale model is a nonlinear, non-local Fokker- Planck equation, that the Gini Coefficient is a Lyapounov functional for this equation, and that the model exhibits a Pareto-type steady state when redistribution is introduced.

(1) the Gini coefficient tends to one in the absence of redistribution; (2) redistribution reduces the Gini coefficient to a level consistent with a steady state similar Pareto's Law; (3) the Gini coefficients of the steady states are independent of the parameter of redistribution; and (4) the Gini-coefficient is a Lyapuonv functional in the absence of wealth redistribution.

(1) In the absence of wealth redistribution, the Gini coefficient of wealth inequality in the YSM is a Lyapuonv functional that tends to one as time tends to infinity, corresponding to maximal wealth inequality; and (2) In the presence of a one-parameter model for wealth redistribution, the YSM exhibits a phase transition in which wealth inequality tends to zero as redistribution tends to zero.
